did_you_know.text: The chapter opens by directly connecting the psalmist’s love for the LORD with the fact that the LORD hears his voice and his pleas.
The psalmist describes his distress through vivid images: the cords of death, the anguish of the grave, trouble, and sorrow.
The LORD is described through three central qualities: gracious, righteous, and compassionate. This description emphasizes both his lovingkindness and his justice.
The expression “protects the inexperienced” presents the LORD as one who watches over the inexperienced or vulnerable. The psalmist testifies about himself: “I was brought low, and he saved me.”
The deliverance is described in three ways: the LORD rescued his soul from death, his eyes from tears, and his feet from stumbling and falling.
The psalmist connects faith with speech: “I believed, therefore I spoke.” His faith is expressed by speaking and turning to the LORD.
In haste and distress, the psalmist said, “Everyone is a liar.” The verse presents his deep feelings during the crisis without specifying exactly whom he meant.
“The cup of salvation” appears as part of the psalmist’s response of thanksgiving, together with calling on the name of the LORD.
The psalmist promises to fulfill his vows to the LORD “in the presence of all his people,” meaning that he will keep them publicly before the community.
The chapter ends in a public and holy setting: in the courts of the LORD’s house in Jerusalem, with the call, “Praise the LORD.”
